title: Dominic and the Cover
premise: Orsen Marchetti, a mid-level financial-crimes investigator who has spent two decades laundering his conscience through procedure, receives a calendar invite from his handler — dead for three days. The meeting pulls him into an off-book extraction: smuggle out Elena Vasquez-Roth, a defector carrying proof that the very agency funding Orsen's career has been washing cartel money through its own compliance division. As Orsen and Elena run a gauntlet of compromised colleagues and a hunter who knows his tradecraft better than he does, he discovers Elena may be bait in a larger trap to expose everyone who ever touched the ledger — including him. In the end, Orsen chooses love and found family over institutional survival, burning the ledger publicly at the cost of his name, his pension, and his old life, walking away with Elena and the ragtag team of exiles who helped them.
about_author: Ansel Villalobos is a former bank-compliance officer from El Paso who spent eleven years tracing money he was never allowed to name before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals discovering the machinery they serve was never neutral.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Three days after his handler Marcus Hale's funeral, Orsen gets a calendar invite from Marcus's still-active account for 9 a.m. tomorrow. He goes despite every instinct, finding an empty conference room, a burner phone taped under the table, and one instruction: 'Elena. Thursday. You're the only clean pair of hands left.' The beat is dread dressed as routine.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback-woven. We see his twenty years of rule-following: flagging accounts, burying suspicions, the quiet erosion of his marriage and ideals. His ex-wife's parting line — 'you launder yourself every morning' — echoes as he decides, against policy, to keep the burner. Emotional beat: a man realizing obedience was always a choice.

chapters.title: Thursday, Vienna
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. In a Vienna safehouse, defector Elena Vasquez-Roth waits for an extraction team that isn't coming; her handler was killed en route. She copies the ledger onto three drives, hides two, and swallows her fear when a knock comes — it's not the enemy yet, but a stranger claiming Orsen sent him. Beat: controlled terror.

chapters.title: The Only Clean Pair of Hands
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen decodes the burner's dead-drop instructions and realizes the extraction plan routes through his own compliance division — meaning someone inside wants Elena found. He contacts Dez Okafor, a disgraced ex-colleague running a failing bar, the closest thing he has to a friend. Beat: reluctant alliance forming.

chapters.title: Hunter's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. Introduce Callum Reeve, the agency's internal-security hunter, working the same case from the other side. Reeve doesn't believe Elena is a traitor; he believes she's chum, and his job is letting the shark surface. He maps Orsen's travel patterns and smiles at how predictable rule-followers are. Beat: cold professional menace.

chapters.title: The Bar With No Name
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. Dez agrees to help, mostly because Orsen once buried a report that would have destroyed him. They assemble a ragtag crew: Priya, a hacker Orsen once reported (and secretly protected), and Tomas, a retired smuggler who owes Marcus. Beat: found family assembling itself out of debts and guilt.

chapters.title: Three Drives
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena meets the fake extraction team, senses the wrongness — wrong shoes, wrong radio cadence — and bolts, going dark in Vienna's transit system. She contacts the number Marcus gave her: Orsen's burner. First contact between them, all tradecraft and no trust. Beat: survival instinct over hope.

chapters.title: Protocol Ghost
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen and Elena arrange a meet using Marcus's old protocols, which only they both know — proof Marcus trusted them both. At the meet, Reeve's surveillance nearly catches them; Priya spoofs the cameras. Orsen sees the ledger data for the first time and recognizes his own division's account numbers. Beat: vertigo of betrayal.

chapters.title: What Marcus Knew
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Interleaved: Marcus's final week (his POV via recovered notes) and Orsen reading them. Marcus discovered the agency was the cartel's bank, planned to blow it open, and named Orsen as the one person too boring to suspect. Orsen understands he was chosen not despite his smallness but because of it. Beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Bait Theory
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. Reeve confronts Orsen in a parking garage, offering him a deal: walk away, keep the pension, let Elena be 'processed.' He confirms Elena might be bait — the directorate may have let her defect deliberately to map the whole resistance network. Orsen can no longer tell if saving her is duty or suicide. Beat: poisoned doubt.

chapters.title: Trust Exercises
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena admits she may have been played — her defection was suspiciously easy, her handler conveniently dead. Orsen tells her he'll help her anyway: 'If you're bait, we cut the line.' Their partnership hardens into something warmer during a night hiding in Tomas's boatyard. Beat: love kindling inside distrust.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Second Half
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya decrypts the second drive and finds names — including judges, senators, and Marcus's killer's cover identity. But the file is a honeypot: opening it pinged a server. Reeve now knows their location. Beat: triumph flipping instantly to alarm.

chapters.title: Boatyard Firefight
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A wet-work team hits the boatyard at dawn. Tomas holds the dock with a shotgun and old habits; Dez takes a graze getting Priya out; Orsen and Elena escape by water. Tomas stays behind to buy time and doesn't make the boat. Beat: first blood, first real loss.

chapters.title: Grief in Transit
chapters.summary: Dez's POV. On a freight train south, the survivors mourn Tomas and argue: use the ledger to negotiate immunity, or publish it and burn everything? Orsen argues for publishing; Dez calls it ego disguised as principle. Elena quietly sides with Orsen. Beat: family fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: The Director's Offer
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Summoned via official channels, Orsen meets Deputy Director Wren, who reveals the full architecture: the agency built the laundering pipeline, Marcus found it, and Elena was seeded as a tripwire. Wren offers Orsen everything — reinstatement, protection, absolution — if he delivers Elena and the drives. Beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Rules
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, interior chapter. Orsen walks his old city, auditing his life like a balance sheet: what obedience bought, what it cost. He visits Marcus's grave, leaves the burner on the headstone, and makes his decision. He texts Dez one word: 'Publish.' Beat: quiet, irreversible resolve.

chapters.title: Cutting the Line
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The team executes the plan: Priya splits the ledger into fragments routed through forty newsrooms simultaneously, timed release so no single kill stops it. Reeve traces the upload node and closes in. Elena insists on being visible — bait works both ways, and she intends to draw Wren's hunters while the files fly. Beat: audacity as armor.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Climax begins: Orsen pretends to accept Wren's deal, delivering 'Elena' to a handoff site — actually Priya's deepfake decoy. Reeve, watching, realizes the con and must choose: obey Wren or follow the truth he's suspected all along. Beat: high-wire tension, masks slipping.

chapters.title: Reeve's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Reeve's POV. Reeve turns, feeding Orsen Wren's location instead of stopping him — 'I hunt liars. She's the biggest.' Together they corner Wren as the ledger publishes worldwide. Wren's countermove: a kill order on everyone present. Gunfire, chaos, Wren dead by her own security detail's confusion. Beat: climax detonating.

chapters.title: Aftermath Accounting
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The ledger is public; investigations bloom; Elena's name is cleared but her old life is ash. Reeve vanishes into unofficial retirement. Dez and Priya regroup at the bar, which suddenly has customers again. Orsen is officially a fugitive and privately free. Beat: exhausted, unheroic relief.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen surrenders to authorities on his own terms, trading testimony for the team's immunity — Elena's included. He accepts disbarment from the service, the loss of everything his twenty years bought. Visiting him before sentencing, Elena says the life they'll build won't have a pension. He says it never really did. Beat: paying the bill without regret.

chapters.title: A Clean Pair of Hands
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Elena's POV. Eighteen months later: a coastal town, a small bookkeeping shop with honest clients, Dez tending bar next door, Priya's postcards arriving from everywhere. Orsen, sentence served, walks up the road home. Elena watches him come and finally lets herself believe survival can cost something and still be worth it. Beat: earned peace, found family complete.
